title: Counterexample learning returns success without persisting feedback
evidence: The public learn_from_failure function promises persistence in its docstring (18), but its entire implementation is logger.info followed by return True (20-21); it is re-exported by verification/__init__.py.
trigger: A caller invokes learn_from_failure with a verification counterexample expecting the documented durable feedback.
impact: The caller receives success although no cortex memory operation occurs; feedback disappears when logging is disabled or logs expire. No active production caller was established.

title: Canonical event serialization is ambiguous for delimiter-bearing fields
evidence: serialize_canonical concatenates event_id, comma-joined parents, tick, payload and signature using unescaped delimiters.
trigger: Two otherwise identical events with payload/signature pairs (a|b,c) and (a,b|c).
impact: Both serialize to the same canonical bytes and graph digest despite different event content; the reference cannot serve as an integrity oracle.

title: Exported global hash does not bind artifact state
evidence: global_hash is SHA256 of the constant bytes artifact_state_v3; program and canonical_graph are not included.
trigger: Export different programs or ledger states through B60MinimalVM.export_artifact.
impact: Every manifest has the same global_hash, preventing consumers of this example field from detecting artifact substitution.

title: Reference CLI announces proof dispatch that never occurs
evidence: static_proof at lines 114-116 is pass; export_artifact returns only in-memory values, while CLI prints Proof IR extracted. Dispatched to Lean/Coq Backends.
trigger: Run any non-HALTED reference program.
impact: Example output misrepresents absent formal verification as completed proof generation and dispatch. No production proof bypass is alleged.

title: FD exhaustion test also passes when target operation succeeds
evidence: Descriptor duplication stops after 5001 even if exhaustion was not reached; the only result assertion is inside if let Err(e) = res.
trigger: Run with a soft descriptor limit above the fixed duplication cap.
impact: Test can report success without entering EMFILE or validating failure under actual exhaustion, leaving the named failure path untested.

title: BLE discovery filters on characteristic UUID instead of advertised service
evidence: Architecture line 29 identifies service 0000180d... and characteristic 00002a37...; scanner instead searches service_uuids for HR_MEASUREMENT_UUID (00002a37...).
trigger: A standard heart-rate device advertises the 0x180d service described by this same document.
impact: The supplied daemon example does not discover the intended device and returns Emisor no encontrado.

title: Cross-device rejection test compares a device ID with itself
evidence: test_nemesis_v12_mount_boundary_exdev_fail_closed asserts q.dev == q.dev and checks only the display string of a constructed CrossDeviceUnsupported error. It never supplies a different mount or invokes an operation expected to return EXDEV.
trigger: A regression removes cross-device rejection from the backend.
impact: This named security regression test still passes because none of its assertions exercise the rejection behavior.

title: Concurrent revocation test asserts a locally manufactured abort
evidence: The revocation thread stores true and is joined before the branch; the true branch constructs EffectTxState::Aborted and asserts it equals itself. It neither revokes an orchestrator authority nor dispatches a guarded operation.
trigger: A regression disables actual revocation enforcement.
impact: test_nemesis_v09_concurrent_capability_revocation remains green without testing revocation or any concurrent operation against the orchestrator. The simulation is labelled in a comment but cannot support the suite security-coverage claim.

title: Malformed tool arguments terminate the stdio server
evidence: process_request invokes handler(params) without exception handling; run_stdio lines 1454-1461 also has no exception boundary. _tool_query_ledger converts an arbitrary string limit using int() at lines 1009-1010; _read_message calls json.loads at line 613 without a parse-error handler.
trigger: Send tools/call for bft_query_ledger with arguments.limit="invalid", or send malformed JSON over the connected stdio transport.
impact: An input validation error escapes the main loop and kills the MCP process, interrupting subsequent legitimate requests instead of returning a per-request error.

title: Lamport allocation races across browser agent connections
evidence: _next_lamport_t lines 39-44 reads MAX(lamport_t)+1 before the separate INSERT at lines 54-60. The schema lines 13-21 has no unique constraint on lamport_t. URLCacheSync opens connect_sync; database/core.py:70 uses isolation_level=None.
trigger: Two BrowserResearchAgent instances sharing a database both read the same MAX before either inserts an attestation.
impact: Both inserts can persist the same logical tick, violating the declared Lamport ordering and leaving no deterministic per-event ordering.

title: Cache commits before the attestation and hides interrupted writes
evidence: cache.put is called at line 120 and _record_attestation only at line 125. URLCacheSync uses the autocommit connection (database/core.py:70). The cache-hit return at lines 87-95 neither checks nor repairs bft_attestations.
trigger: The process exits, or the attestation INSERT fails, after cache.put has committed and before the attestation is persisted.
impact: Subsequent calls return cached content marked passed without the promised audit record, and normal cache hits never recover that missing record.

title: Conformity simulator authorizes CE marking even when checks fail
evidence: overall_status at line 148 depends on all_passed, but market_access_declaration is unconditionally CE_MARKING_AUTHORIZED at line 149; audit_sitrep returns False when SITREP is absent (49-51), and generate_annex_vi_pack still writes the declaration (164-165).
trigger: Run this explicitly labelled simulator with a missing SITREP or any failing checklist.
impact: The generated example declaration asserts authorization while recording NON_CONFORMANT, creating a contradictory output that cannot support the claimed marking. This is an example artifact issue, not evidence of a production legal approval flow.

title: Conformity example labels a status string as verified hardware evidence
evidence: Lines 82-87 check only whether ROOT-named tasks have attestation.status == ATTESTED_BY_OPERATOR. No signature, trusted key or payload binding is checked; line 95 nevertheless emits Hardware (Secure Enclave P-256) validada, and line 96 takes a signature substring without verification.
trigger: Provide a SITREP ROOT task with the expected status string and an arbitrary or absent signature.
impact: The example marks human-supervision evidence PASS and claims validated hardware without authenticating any evidence. Simulator labeling limits the scope but does not make that evidence statement accurate.

title: Flagship prerequisite check prints the API token
evidence: The documented Check with shell block echoes CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN using its full current value when set.
trigger: Follow the prerequisite instructions with a real token in the environment, especially via a terminal tool whose output is logged.
impact: The credential is copied into terminal history/transcripts or agent tool output although only presence needs checking. No actual credential was read during this audit.

title: Audio example mutates persistent DSP state during rendering
evidence: Line 36 memoizes a mutable ballisticState once; lines 53-56 pass it into extractBands on every render. SpectralFlux.ts:95-99 overwrites prevSpectrum and applies ballistics; :51-60 incorporates and updates smoothedValues.
trigger: Render the same frame after a different preceding frame, seek backwards, or rerender the same component/frame.
impact: Onset and smoothed band values depend on render history rather than only frame and input audio. Preview seeking and independently rendered segments can produce differing camera and glow values for the same frame.

title: Audit workers approve source without reading or checking it
evidence: Worker only calls os.stat and sleeps, then emits APPROVED with exergy=21000 for nonempty files (21–32). Final verdict unconditionally says TOPOLOGÍA INTACTA / RFO=0 (78).
trigger: Run the advertised audit on any nonempty malformed or unsafe source.
impact: Output represents file existence/size as an affirmative audit verdict and fabricated quality metric.

title: Commit linter inspects working tree instead of staged bytes
evidence: Names come from git diff --cached (8), but grep reads "$FILE" in working tree (19–42). Loop also word-splits filenames (17).
trigger: Stage a violation and remove it only in the working tree, or stage a source filename containing spaces.
impact: The advertised precommit gate can approve staged violations or skip their real path; no active hook integration is asserted.

title: Non-Darwin arm reports anti-debug protection despite skipping it
evidence: enforce_anti_debug returns immediately when platform != darwin (43–44), yet arm unconditionally sets antidebug_ok=True (69–74). tests/test_c5_memory_shield.py:54 asserts True on every platform.
trigger: Call arm on Linux.
impact: Audit status claims anti-debug protection was armed although no anti-debug mechanism ran.

title: Concurrent sign-offs can fork the audit hash chain
evidence: register_sign_off reads the latest digest before the INSERT transaction; verify_ledger_integrity requires every row to reference the immediately preceding row.
trigger: Two VerificationGate connections using the same database read the same latest digest before either inserts.
impact: Both inserts can commit with the same predecessor; subsequent integrity verification rejects the otherwise legitimate audit chain.

title: Enterprise PoC reports success without asserting verifier outcomes
evidence: run_cmd returns returncode; lines 152 and 166 assign code but do not check it; lines 170-175 unconditionally print successful completion and compliance assertions.
trigger: The verifier incorrectly accepts the modified chain, or verification exits with an unrelated error while the ledger file exists.
impact: The example still claims successful tamper rejection and compliance, hiding the regression being demonstrated.

title: TLA liveness comments claim a physical deadline absent from the model
evidence: Spec uses weak fairness and Termination is eventual state completion; no clock, deadline, bounded delay, or physical-time constant is modeled.
trigger: Readers use the advertised termination in T seconds or absence of network deadlocks as an operational guarantee.
impact: Unbounded eventual progress under assumed fairness is presented as bounded physical termination, overstating the proof scope.

title: Backward conditioning uses the initial prior at the wrong timestep
evidence: For target_t < min(window), joint = pi0 * T_steps[:, observed] uses pi0 directly; it does not propagate pi0 to target_t.
trigger: pi0 describes timestep zero, target_t is positive, and the earliest observation is later than target_t in a nonstationary Markov chain.
impact: Posterior probabilities, hallucination rates and surprisal can be incorrect. The prior must first be advanced to the target timestep or its time origin made explicit.

title: Concurrent audit appends can fork the hash chain
evidence: Lines 63–71 read the previous tail and compute the next digest before the independent append at lines 73–74; no lock serializes those operations.
trigger: Two pipe_audit processes read the same ledger tail before either appends.
impact: Both new entries name the same predecessor, so the sequential ledger chain breaks under ordinary concurrent auditing; valid activity becomes indistinguishable from a damaged chain. This concerns the audit trail, not a demonstrated execution bypass.

title: Malformed action fields raise instead of returning rejection
evidence: Lines 47–51 call int on untrusted payload values, but the handler at line 55 catches only ValueError and KeyError. int(None) and int([]) raise TypeError.
trigger: Call verify_payload with both action_class and agent_id present and agent_id=None (or a numeric field containing a list), using an otherwise recognized action class.
impact: The boolean verification API propagates an exception rather than returning False; consumers expecting deterministic rejection can fail a request/task. No protected-effect consumer or authorization bypass was established.

title: Annex VI theorem claims legal guarantees absent from its model
evidence: Lines 7–11 claim impossibility of fraud/noncompliance. Lines 16–31 model only four caller-supplied Bool values; theorem lines 37–49 merely decomposes their conjunction. Lines 55–60 hard-code all four values true without checking any document, signature or log.
trigger: Use this demo/theorem as evidence for the stated legal or cryptographic compliance claim.
impact: A tautology over asserted flags is presented as a guarantee about external evidence; forged evidence with all flags asserted is outside the theorem and cannot be ruled out by it. Finding concerns proof scope and documentation, not a legal determination.

title: Gateway fallback example calls an undeclared Anthropic provider
evidence: The fenced example imports createAiGateway, createOpenAI and generateText and defines only openai, then invokes anthropic(...) in its fallback array. No Anthropic import or initialization exists in the file.
trigger: Adapt the advertised automatic fallback block using the preceding imports and provider setup.
impact: TypeScript reports an unresolved identifier (or JavaScript throws ReferenceError); the documented fallback example cannot run as shown.

title: Memory JSON is truncated in place without atomic replacement
evidence: _write_json opens each destination with mode w; no temporary replacement or fsync. crystallize_session writes project, ghosts and system separately at lines 113,129,155.
trigger: Process interruption or write failure after opening a memory file, or between the three writes.
impact: Previously valid memory can become empty/partial, and the three ledgers can disagree; the next read kills the process instead of recovering.

title: Concurrent session consolidation loses completed updates
evidence: Project read-modify-write spans lines 87–113; ghosts and system repeat the same pattern without locking or version checks.
trigger: Two CLI invocations or ledger instances consolidate concurrently after reading the same initial JSON.
impact: The later writer overwrites the other session changes, decisions or session log entries.

title: UTC clock values are mislabeled with a +02:00 offset
evidence: datetime.now(timezone.utc) is formatted with the literal suffix +02:00 without timezone conversion.
trigger: Any call to crystallize_session.
impact: Persisted timestamps represent an instant two hours earlier than the actual event and cannot reliably be correlated with real UTC events.

title: Zero-operation benchmark indexes an empty latency vector
evidence: CLI accepts std::stoull(argv[1]); when total_ops is 0 neither loop records samples, yet percentile indexing and back() are unconditional.
trigger: Run the standalone benchmark with argument 0.
impact: Undefined behavior or crash instead of rejecting invalid benchmark input.

title: Advertised decision latency excludes receipt signing
evidence: t1 is captured before _sign_decision; latency_ns=t1-t0 is reported as decision latency although route signs and constructs the result afterward. The opening claim includes cryptographic receipts and a decision-latency target.
trigger: Use the PoC latency distribution to evaluate the complete route call against its advertised target.
impact: Reported figures omit HMAC/SHA3 work and cannot establish the claimed end-to-end decision latency.

title: Malformed CRL files silently become certificate-ID literals
evidence: parse_crl_arg catches every JSON/read exception and falls back to splitting the original file path (lines 78-81); main passes that list to verify_compliance_certificate at 118-123. standalone_verify.py:713 only revokes when certificate_id occurs in that list.
trigger: An explicitly supplied CRL file is truncated, invalid JSON, or cannot be read while the certificate otherwise validates.
impact: The CLI can report a revoked certificate valid because the requested revocation source was ignored without error. Fail closed for file parse/read/schema errors.

title: Proposal endpoint reports postconditions VERIFIED without checking an effect
evidence: Lines 881-898 inspect only optional simulated_execution_result, and actual_file_sha256 defaults to the reported value. Lines 900-909 unconditionally emit VERIFIED, independent-verifier evidence and postconditions_checked despite effects_executed=0. cortex_mcp_server.py:1412-1418 returns this payload directly; effect_dispatch.py:56 categorizes this endpoint as read-only.
trigger: A caller proposes a validated mutation with matching caller-supplied pre-hashes and omits simulated_execution_result.
impact: MCP consumers receive false verification evidence for a proposal with no independently observed postcondition. This finding concerns returned assurance; no native execution authorization bypass is established.

title: Directory linter skips arbitrary source paths containing build or dist
evidence: audit_directory tests ignored substrings against the entire root path and returns no violations for skipped roots; main lines 157-159 prints compliance and exits zero for an empty result.
trigger: Audit a source tree under a path such as /tmp/build-review/src or /tmp/distribution-ui containing frontend violations.
impact: All matching directories silently escape inspection and the tool reports compliance. Match directory components and report empty coverage explicitly.

title: Require digest coverage for every required evidence file
evidence: signed_file_digests defaults to {}; only supplied entries are hashed at lines 904–924. required_rel_files is checked for existence only. CLI consumes valid as PASS and exit 0 (verifier/cli.py:89–95).
trigger: A pack has a signed envelope omitting claims.json, scope.json, regulatory matrix or other required files from file_digests.
impact: Omitted files can be changed without invalidating signature/checksums; checksums_valid can still be true and mutable claims affect final verdict.

title: Reject an empty execution trace for a nonempty ledger
evidence: All count/hash comparisons are nested under if trace_lines; an empty trace skips the promised cross-check.
trigger: Pack contains a nonempty valid ledger and an empty execution-trace.jsonl with matching updated signed file digest.
impact: Verifier reports evidence verifiable despite no execution trace corresponding to the ledger.

title: Recompute JSON event hashes before declaring integrity verified
evidence: When an event dictionary has entry_hash/hash, only that supplied hash enters leaves; remaining event fields are ignored. The result sets integrity_verified true. verify_compliance_certificate uses this result at lines 728–740.
trigger: Change payload fields in an exported JSON event while retaining its entry_hash and certificate Merkle root.
impact: Certificate verification can still succeed although event contents were changed; the documented recomputation and integrity guarantee do not hold for JSON evidence.

title: Remove the shared bearer credential from the launchd template
evidence: Plist embeds a literal bearer credential. tools/babylon60_mcp.py:975–996 reads this environment variable and :873 compares incoming authorization to it. Credential value intentionally omitted.
trigger: Deploy this launchd template unchanged.
impact: Anyone with repository/template access knows the bearer credential for that deployment; loopback limits network reach but does not make the shared value secret. No deployment or exploitation was tested.

title: Cache audit resolves benchmark below scripts instead of repository root
evidence: Two dirname calls on scripts/c5_quality_gates/run_cache_audit.py produce scripts/. Lines 26-27 then select scripts/tests/cache_kinetic_benchmark.cpp; targeted file inventory locates source at tests/cache_kinetic_benchmark.cpp.
trigger: Run the documented cache audit runner from the repository.
impact: Compilation receives a nonexistent source path and the audit exits before collecting benchmark evidence.

title: Single-chunk ledger example accepts an invalid chunk
evidence: verifyLedgerStream returns true for [_] regardless of deltaValid; only the two-or-more branch calls verifyChunkBoundary, which checks validity.
trigger: Apply the canonical example to a singleton Chunk with deltaValid=false.
impact: The documented verifier accepts a ledger explicitly marked invalid. This is an example defect; no production consumer or deployed bypass is asserted.

title: Exported MemoryStore silently drops all writes
evidence: MemoryStore.set is pass (lines 47-48); get unconditionally returns None (44-45). The class is exported in __all__. Targeted search found no current internal caller.
trigger: A consumer imports the public MemoryStore API, calls set and subsequently get.
impact: The write reports no failure and data cannot be retrieved; the public persistence-looking API cannot preserve state. No active internal data-loss path is claimed.

title: Effective resistance silently treats disconnected graphs as finite
evidence: The function accepts arbitrary nx.Graph, checks only node count, and always returns N*trace(pinv(L)). For two isolated vertices L and pinv(L) are zero, so the returned total resistance is zero although no intervertex conduction path exists.
trigger: Call compute_effective_resistance, or get_structural_debt_triple, on a disconnected graph with at least two vertices.
impact: Disconnected structure is assigned a finite, potentially zero total resistance and misleading structural-debt output. Scope is the exported analytical function; no control-policy consumer is asserted.

title: Cache report unconditionally claims mitigation and patentability
evidence: The runner writes a fixed conclusion asserting complete L1 false-sharing mitigation and technical patentability after any exit-zero benchmark. It neither parses measurements nor checks a threshold or environment.
trigger: After fixing the path issue, benchmark exits zero even when results do not show the expected performance improvement.
impact: Generated evidence states success independent of measured results and makes a patentability assertion unsupported by the benchmark.

title: Dependency validation and revocation are separated from insertion by unlocked transactions
evidence: add_record commits dependency checks at 468, appends ledger at 471, then inserts edges in a new transaction at 495-568. revoke_record snapshots closure and commits at 639 before its updates at 663-680. query_active_memories filters only record status, not upstream status (848-859).
trigger: An add validates ACTIVE parent; concurrent revoke snapshots existing children and revokes parent; add then inserts its child and edges. Alternatively a child is added after the revocation closure snapshot.
impact: The new child remains ACTIVE and retrievable despite its revoked dependency, outside the revocation closure. These are synchronous methods but independent engines/threads/processes use separate SQLite connections.

title: Ledger acknowledgement precedes durable memory-state mutation without recovery
evidence: revoke_record commits MEMORY_RECORD_REVOKED through append_event before opening the mutation transaction at 663. Ledger append commits independently (cortex_persist_ledger.py:257-271); engine constructor only initializes schema, without projection replay. add_record and retract_attribution use the same pattern.
trigger: Process stops or the second database transaction fails after ledger append succeeds and before memory updates commit.
impact: A durable revocation receipt can coexist with an ACTIVE readable record after reopening; committed additions can lack their memory projection. No runtime execution was performed.

title: Revocation silently truncates dependency closure after 1024 levels
evidence: Recursive closure uses c.depth < 1024; add_record accepts arbitrarily deep acyclic dependency chains. The returned total_invalidated does not signal truncation. Retraction has the same bound at 1062-1075.
trigger: Create an acyclic dependency chain deeper than 1024 and revoke its root.
impact: Nodes beyond the bound remain ACTIVE and retain their blobs; advertised transitive revocation is incomplete.

title: Policy epoch rolls back on engine restart
evidence: __init__ unconditionally initializes _host_epoch to 1; advance_policy_epoch (333-340) updates only this instance field. add_record signs and records using that field, while get_record accepts stored epoch without comparing a persistent host minimum.
trigger: Advance epoch above 1, reopen MemoryGovernanceEngine on the same database, register principal key, then create a record.
impact: New records are issued under epoch 1 despite previously advancing the authoritative epoch, contradicting monotonic policy governance.

title: Python-only counter loop is described as Rust FFI and SPMC validation
evidence: Header claims lock-free Python/Rust coupling; FFIWriter constructs a local ctypes structure (42), never loads a Rust library or starts a reader; run_stress_test only publishes sequentially and asserts counter parity (76-97). _pack_=1 is also not a cache-line alignment guarantee.
trigger: Use this demo success as evidence for the declared cross-language seqlock/SPMC property.
impact: The example cannot establish ABI coupling, concurrent reader coherence or lock-free ordering. No production caller was located by targeted search; finding is confined to example/evidence claims.

title: Example formal gate approves a truthy field without checking a proof
evidence: audit_ast_closure only checks truthiness of formal_proof and claim/premise overlap, then hashes repr and returns PENDING_ATTESTATION at 77-78. The surrounding text presents it as deterministic formal closure validation.
trigger: Supply a nonempty arbitrary formal_proof string with empty claims/premises to the shown example.
impact: The documented routine accepts an unverified proof and labels it ready for attestation. Targeted consumer search found only this documentation definition; this is not a demonstrated production authorization bypass.

title: Folder prefix example uses an unbounded lexical lower bound
evidence: The documented starts-with filter contains only operator gte, value docs/api/, with no upper bound or separate prefix predicate.
trigger: Apply the example to a collection also containing lexically later unrelated folders, such as docs/zzz/ or private/.
impact: A greater-than-or-equal comparison does not enforce the claimed prefix and can include unrelated retrieval results. This is a docs/example filter defect, not a demonstrated tenant authorization boundary.

title: Differential comparison reads both artifacts after the Rust run
evidence: Rust .output() completes at lines 31-33 before py_ir is read at line 47; rs_ir is then read from the same artifact_bundle_v3/proof.ir at line 51. src/babylon60.rs:594 writes that path. Cargo.toml:76-77 registers this test.
trigger: Reference interpreter exists and both commands complete successfully.
impact: The comparison can hash the Rust-produced artifact twice and pass despite a different Python trace. Currently the missing reference/interpreter.py also causes an early successful return at lines 15-18.

title: Preflight suppresses compilation failure and still approves
evidence: cargo check failure is consumed by || echo; the script continues to its unconditional APPROVED message and exit 0 when the following script returns success.
trigger: cargo check exits nonzero while enforce_c5_rules.sh returns zero.
impact: Callers receive successful environment validation for a workspace that did not compile.

title: Environment preflight also changes remote branch protection
evidence: The environment validation calls ./scripts/enforce_c5_rules.sh, whose lines 17-37 execute gh api --method PUT on /repos/borjamoskv/BABYLON-60/branches/main/protection, with no opt-in argument.
trigger: A user runs preflight with an authenticated gh account able to administer the repository.
impact: A routine validation invocation can change remote review and branch-protection policy. This is a traced side effect, not evidence that it has occurred.

title: Auditor follows file symlinks when rewriting targets
evidence: collect_targets accepts item.is_file() at line 60; audit_file uses stat/read_text/write_text at lines 75,83,101 without rejecting symlinks or checking target containment. run_swarm forwards collected paths with dry_run false by default.
trigger: A matching-extension symlink inside the audited tree points to a writable outside file containing a case variant of one replacement term, and the CLI runs without --dry-run.
impact: The advertised workspace audit can modify a file outside the selected root through the symlink.

title: Codex query reports success after a failed execution with partial text
evidence: Failure is returned only when proc.returncode != 0 AND not full_text; every other path returns success True at line 169. _parse_codex_events does not propagate failed turn events.
trigger: Codex emits an agent_message then exits nonzero, for example after a later tool or turn failure.
impact: Consumers receive success True with partial output and lose the execution failure signal.

title: Tenant example treats a lower bound as prefix isolation
evidence: The Multitenancy example has only folder gte tenants/${tenantId}/ and calls it a starts-with pattern. Official Cloudflare filtering documentation defines gte as greater-than-or-equal and requires an upper bound for folder prefix matching: https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/configuration/retrieval/filtering/ ; legacy format documentation also requires two range bounds: https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/api/migration/autorag-filter-format/ .
trigger: A developer adapts the multitenancy example to an API accepting its filter shape in an index shared across tenants.
impact: A lexically later tenant folder satisfies the lone lower bound; this example is insufficient to isolate tenant retrieval. Current APIs may reject this older filter shape instead. No active deployed consumer was established.

title: Compiler README links resolve outside the repository root targets
evidence: Links ../../../proof/lean/BabylonTrace.lean and ../../../CLAIMS.toml resolve to 00_ABZU_KERNEL/proof/lean/BabylonTrace.lean and 00_ABZU_KERNEL/CLAIMS.toml, rather than root proof/lean and CLAIMS.toml; the same prefix occurs on line 7.
trigger: Reader follows proof or claims links from the compiler README.
impact: The documented evidence links do not point to the intended root proof and claims files.

title: Idle eviction uses tenant age instead of inactivity
evidence: idle_time = now - scope.created_at; TenantScope.created_at is set only when registering a new tenant. AgencyHypervisor.project_event does not update an activity timestamp.
trigger: Call evaluate_and_evict after max_idle_seconds while the tenant continues processing events.
impact: The active tenant is deleted by evict_tenant despite recent activity; subsequent project_event calls return False and its in-memory queue loses registration. This is an API-level defect; no deployed scheduler was established.

title: Tip-of-tongue branch is mathematically unreachable
evidence: highest_score initializes to 0.5 and only increases. tip_of_tongue requires highest_score < 0.35 and a nonempty matched list; matches themselves require a score > 0.5.
trigger: Any call to judge_procedural_fok with candidates.
impact: The returned judgment can never signal tip_of_tongue, so callers cannot distinguish this intended uncertainty state. No downstream authorization consequence is claimed.

title: Drizzle example shadows the table with the query result
evidence: const users = await db.select().from(users).where(eq(users.active, true)).limit(10); declares users and reads the same binding in its initializer. The snippet also lacks imports for eq and the users schema.
trigger: Copy the Drizzle example into a Worker handler and evaluate the query.
impact: JavaScript encounters the users temporal dead zone (or TypeScript rejects the declaration), preventing the documented query from executing. Use a separate result variable and import the schema and eq.

title: Inference verifier proves only a freely chosen multiplication witness
evidence: verify_inference_payload verifies InferenceConstraint; build.rs:8-16 constrains only private weight * public nonce == public expected_hash. No model, input, output or authorized weight commitment is constrained. stress_test.rs:29-45 constructs proofs of precisely this relation.
trigger: A consumer interprets true from verify_inference_payload as evidence of model inference. For every nonzero nonce and field hash a witness weight = hash / nonce exists.
impact: A valid proof establishes no inference correctness or binding to a particular model. Only the local verifier and stress harness were traced; no production effect bypass is claimed.

title: Groth16 setup randomness is publicly reproducible
evidence: get_verifying_key seeds ChaCha20Rng with a literal public constant and runs Groth16::setup; src/bin/stress_test.rs:19-26 regenerates the same setup for its prover.
trigger: This verifying key is used as a security boundary beyond an isolated demonstration.
impact: Setup secret randomness can be reconstructed by any party; this cannot provide the secret setup assumptions of Groth16. No forged proof was generated in this audit.

title: Claim pending messages atomically before delivering them
evidence: pull_messages SELECTs pending rows at 160-170 and later UPDATEs selected IDs at 198-205, without BEGIN IMMEDIATE or a conditional pending claim. mcp_server.py:290 exposes this as receive_messages.
trigger: Two consumers pull the same destination concurrently, before either UPDATE commits.
impact: Both can return the same pending messages, causing duplicate handling. This is a static interleaving finding; concurrent execution was not performed.

title: Persistent tunnel connections lower required durability to NORMAL
evidence: Every _get_connection executes PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL; .babylon60rules requires transactional persistence with synchronous=FULL.
trigger: The broker acknowledges a committed message before a system power failure.
impact: Acknowledged WAL commits lack the required FULL synchronization guarantee. The audit did not simulate power loss.

title: Adversarial campaign rejects labels instead of exercising independent gates
evidence: Gate 2 rejects on adversarial_type == INTENT_TAMPERING even without checking evidence. PRECONDITION_MISMATCH and ENTROPIC_SLUDGE modify payload after digest calculation (151-158), so Gate 2 rejects them before gates 3/4; gates 3/4 themselves branch on labels at 199/215.
trigger: Campaign outputs are used to claim the named precondition, Shannon filtering and authority isolation controls were verified.
impact: A 100% rejection report does not establish those controls; two scenarios do not reach their named gates, and the broker is harness-local. This finding concerns test validity, not a production bypass.

title: Do not copy authentication credentials into analytics dimensions
evidence: The full Worker example stores request.headers.get("x-api-key") verbatim as Analytics Engine index1.
trigger: A developer copies the example into a service authenticating with x-api-key.
impact: Raw credentials become analytics records accessible to analytics readers and retained beyond request processing. Use a nonsecret tenant ID or an irreversible identifier. No actual credential was read.

title: Anchor demo announces irreversible Bitcoin anchoring without submitting anything
evidence: run_apex_suite uses four literal simulated receipt bytes (48-53), hashes them and formats a payload; it has no transaction submission, signature verification or timestamp proof. Lines 64-65 announce an irreversible PoW sink and consummated closure.
trigger: The printed success statements are consumed as audit evidence of anchoring or hardware attestation.
impact: The demo output overstates its evidence: it only constructs bytes from simulation data and does not establish Bitcoin inclusion or hardware signatures.

title: Queued claims capture an obsolete predecessor and are silently discarded

title: Software hashes are exported as hardware-sealed TPM quotes

title: Tokenizer cannot encode ordinary Unicode outside Latin-1

trigger: Encode an unseen character such as U+20AC or a CJK character; a single-character training input also adds nothing.

trigger: DNS/TLS/network failure or an HTTP error body instead of the expected range response.

evidence: A counts actor switches on consecutive changes; B/C retain each file owner forever at lines 224-237 rather than the claimed two-change window. title: Derivation creates FormalProof for an unrelated goal

title: IFC parser splits semicolons inside quoted values

trigger: A valid IFC string property contains a semicolon or /*.
impact: Entities are silently lost or corrupted while parse returns Ok, affecting extracted compliance data.

title: Skill persistence reports success after failed copy
evidence: The script uses set -uo pipefail, not errexit; the copytree Python command is not checked and execution proceeds to a separate status=ok JSON emitter.
trigger: Target creation or copying fails due to permissions, disk exhaustion or a concurrent target writer.

title: Setback distance fabricated from local placement axes
evidence: SetbackDistance is populated as min(abs(x), abs(y)) from local placement without property boundary geometry or parent placement composition.
trigger: Building has a translated/rotated parent placement or parcel boundary unrelated to the local axes.
impact: A synthetic numeric setback is exposed as an actual property and can yield incorrect spatial compliance conclusions.

title: Garbage collection totals count repeated scans as reclaimable bytes
evidence: SHARUR_GC_000 and SHARUR_GC_006 repeat the same target/pattern, sample paths and bytes_found=640958858. Similar cycles repeat in all cohorts; total_anergy_bytes aggregates these repeats rather than identifying unique files.
trigger: Use total_anergy_bytes or cohort bytes as a storage evacuation/reclamation estimate.
impact: The historical report overcounts storage by counting the same files across agents; no actual deletion or consumer execution was established.

title: REPL spins indefinitely after stdin reaches EOF
evidence: read_line result is checked only with is_err(); Ok(0) falls through to eval_line of an empty buffer and immediately repeats the loop. CLI declares Repl in main.rs:56.
trigger: Close stdin with Ctrl-D or run the interactive REPL with an exhausted pipe.
impact: Process remains running, repeatedly prints prompts and consumes CPU/output resources.

title: Sexagesimal addition overflows for accepted u64 operands
evidence: User inputs are parsed as unrestricted u64 at lines 53-56; f1 + f2 and s1 + s2 + carry use unchecked arithmetic at 58 and 61.
trigger: sexa add 18446744073709551615 0 1 0, or two maximal fraction operands.
impact: Debug builds panic; release builds can wrap and report an incorrect exact Q60 result.

title: Paper downloader disables HTTPS certificate validation globally
evidence: ssl._create_default_https_context is replaced by ssl._create_unverified_context before urlopen calls at lines 20 and 28.
trigger: Execute this script on a network where HTTPS traffic can be intercepted.
impact: Crossref metadata and downloaded paper bytes can be substituted without certificate errors; imported use also alters later urllib HTTPS behavior in that process.

title: YAML parser strips hash characters inside quoted strings
evidence: re.sub(r"#.*$", "", line_raw) runs before _parse_scalar processes quotes. parse_yaml is publicly reexported by primitives/__init__.py.
trigger: Parse a supported scalar such as color: "#ffffff" or value: "abc#def".
impact: Configuration strings are silently truncated, with quote fragments retained; valid quoted YAML scalar values cannot be represented reliably.

title: Gemini generation tool returns a canned response without invoking Gemini
evidence: The registered gemini_labs_generate tool formats a fixed response_text; GEMINI_API_KEY is read but no API client/request appears anywhere in this module. Result and telemetry label it GEMINI_GENERATE (149-152).
trigger: Invoke gemini_labs_generate with FastMCP installed.
impact: Callers receive a purported generated response independent of prompt content, and the ledger records a model generation that never occurred.

title: Receipt producer labels a public hash prefix as an Ed25519 signature
evidence: signature_ed25519 is the literal prefix sig_ed25519_ plus merkle_root[:32]; no private key/sign operation exists. Both MCP tools return this object (147-152,161-165), and append_auto_log persists it.
trigger: Generate a receipt through either MCP tool.
impact: Returned and persisted receipts cannot provide the advertised signature authentication; anyone can construct that field. No downstream authorization bypass is claimed.

title: Syntax integrity gate omits the primary babylon60 package
evidence: TRACKED_DIRS lists root directories cli/core/etc but omits 01_KISH_ENGINE; enumeration at 23-30 scans only those roots and root-level Python files. Assigned runtime modules live in 01_KISH_ENGINE/babylon60/.
trigger: A SyntaxError is introduced into 01_KISH_ENGINE/babylon60 while this test is used as the advertised every-tracked-module syntax gate.
impact: The advertised structural gate never compiles the primary package and can pass despite syntax errors there.

evidence: publish admits RUNNING->WRITING at 82, then unconditionally stores RUNNING at 91; epistemic_halt independently stores HALTING at 123. Identical content exists in the assigned workspace skill-library copy.
trigger: epistemic_halt runs after publish admission and before its final status store.

evidence: Line 38 specifies invoking epistemic_halt and POISONED after MAX_RETRIES; read instead returns None at 119 without changing status. The workspace skill-library copy is identical.
trigger: A reader reaches MAX_RETRIES while a writer is stalled or contention persists.

title: Synthetic worker scores are presented without a simulation label
evidence: agent_worker only sleeps and derives exergy = 15000.0 + (agent_idx * 17.3) % 6000.0; it then emits verdicts including FALSACIÓN_POPPERIANA and cohort names for hardware/SEP/SMT topics. No corresponding checks occur in this file.
trigger: Running this script and interpreting its JSON cohort_stats/apex_agents as audit evidence.
impact: The output ranks fabricated arithmetic scores as audit verdicts without declaring a simulation, so it cannot support the hardware or security topics it names.

title: Concurrent installer mutations are never followed by an integrity audit
evidence: audit_target_integrities runs before the 10-thread injection phase. After concurrent injections the final success condition checks only return codes and never audits resulting files.
trigger: Parallel installer runs all return zero but leave duplicated, broken, or inconsistent targets.

evidence: BrainCorpusIndex.__init__ never sets index_duration; index() returns immediately when BRAIN_DIR does not exist (107-109), while run_sharur_100_swarm reads corpus.index_duration unconditionally at 739.

impact: AttributeError prevents the audit from producing a report or explicit missing-input result.

title: OpenAI secret detector uses a literal malformed repetition
evidence: The OpenAI pattern ends in [a-zA-Z0-9]{20,T}; the nonnumeric upper repetition bound is not a valid numeric quantifier. The scanning loop at 154-159 relies on this pattern to increment secret_matches.
trigger: A transcript contains an ordinary sk- prefixed credential.
impact: The scanner misses credentials and reports a misleading zero count. No actual credentials were read or reproduced.

title: Audit emits unconditional compliance verdicts without examining evidence
evidence: Agents 21,22,24-27 and many others assign PASS plus fixed compliance metrics without inspecting corpus data; 592-596 invent nominal entropy when no samples exist. Results feed compile_swarm_sitrep (reporters.py:360-381), which counts PASS and computes exergy_score from that count, then emits the reports at auditor.py:774.
trigger: Run the auditor on a corpus with missing entropy samples or violations of the claimed compliance properties.
impact: Generated forensic reports present untested properties as passing and can mask defects in the audited history. This is an evidence-quality defect, not a claim about physical energy or runtime isolation.

title: Polymeter selection is ignored by the generator
evidence: createDialog exposes a fixed-bar versus continuous polymeter mode; apply forwards it, but generate_euclidean never reads mode and always uses BAR // n for both layers.
trigger: Choose Polimetro Continuo in the dialog.
impact: The example produces the same fixed-bar timing as the other selection.

title: Comment stripping corrupts quoted URLs in tsconfig
evidence: JSONC_COMMENT_RE matches // through the end of a line without tracking strings. _load_jsonc applies it before json.loads and suppresses parsing failures as {}. ts_aliases then loses compilerOptions.paths; extract_js classifies unresolved alias imports as external registry candidates.
trigger: A valid tsconfig contains a quoted URL such as a $schema URL and path aliases.
impact: The scanner silently discards valid configuration and may flag working alias imports as phantom external packages.

title: Arithmetic overflow escapes VM fail-closed handling
evidence: mul_scalar multiplies accumulated u128 units without checked_mul and casts seconds to u64; add at line 35 also uses unchecked u64 addition. execute directly calls both. ffi.rs:143-163 exposes execution through extern C without panic handling.
trigger: Repeated SexaMulRational or SexaAdd instructions exceed the seconds range; registers are also public to Rust callers.
impact: Release arithmetic can wrap or truncate and return success with an incorrect result; checked builds panic rather than poisoning the manifest, and panic crossing the C ABI can abort the host process.

title: Out-of-range jumps return successful execution
evidence: Jump assigns the decoded u16 directly to pc; the execute loop only checks pc < bytecode.len() and returns Ok after it ends. Conditional jump branches do the same. ffi.rs:154-160 converts Ok to return code 0.
trigger: Bytecode containing a jump target beyond the supplied buffer.
impact: Malformed control flow is accepted as successful completion with a running manifest, rather than rejected.

title: Forensic report certifies controls without checking them
evidence: Cohort 5 agent 99 unconditionally assigns PASS and ATTESTED_C5_REAL. Agents 64-70 and 83-86 similarly return static security/integrity claims. compile_swarm_sitrep derives an exergy score from PASS count at line 380. Auditor.py:757-779 schedules these functions and persists their results.
trigger: Any invocation of the conversation auditor, including a corpus containing leaks, broken links or divergent files.
impact: Persisted reports falsely attest unchecked controls; the final certification remains PASS regardless of the failed findings in other agents.

title: Stress gate never asserts validation and rejection counts
evidence: The loop counts successful valid calls and rejected invalid calls, but final exit status checks only average latency and memory delta. Invalid calls that return normally are silently accepted.
trigger: A regression makes validate_mcp_contract return True for every input or False for valid inputs without raising.
impact: The stress script can exit 0 and announce success while contract rejection or valid-input acceptance is broken. No physical conclusion follows from these measurements.

title: Bootstrap stores unencrypted private key in encrypted-key column
evidence: generate_identity serializes PKCS8 with NoEncryption at lines 29-33; bootstrap_genesis inserts priv_pem directly into private_key_enc at lines 63-65.
trigger: A caller invokes bootstrap_genesis on an empty ledger.
impact: The resulting database and its backups contain the signing private key in plaintext; access to the database permits key recovery. No active bootstrap caller was located in the targeted package search.

title: Failed email handlers are acknowledged and permanently deduplicated
evidence: is_duplicate inserts the message ID before handlers execute (lines 191-204); lines 255-259 swallow handler exceptions and return status processed; router returns this result at lines 309-310.
trigger: A registered synchronous handler raises while processing a webhook with message_id.
impact: HTTP success suppresses provider retries; an explicit retry is duplicate_skipped for the TTL although the handler never completed. Track completion and report failure before acknowledging.

title: Filesystem event arithmetic overflows before burnout can be observed
evidence: event.paths.len() as u8 * 10 and inferred u8 entropy_injected += surprise_value (lines 45-49) use unchecked narrow arithmetic.
trigger: A single event carries at least 26 paths, or accumulated per-tick path counts exceed 25.
impact: Debug execution panics; release arithmetic wraps and can suppress or lower the injected value, invalidating the demonstrated overload behavior. This is an example, not a finding about the production scheduler.

title: Simulation announces a verified ZK invariant from a synthetic timing comparison
evidence: Lines 10-18 implement a fixed sleep and an always-true hash expression; lines 75-76 call speedup > 50 a surviving O(1) invariant and report no deadlocks. Targeted references found only the local demo definition/call, not a production proof consumer.
trigger: Running the demo where the synthetic sleep/hash ratio exceeds 50.
impact: Output presents timing of a simulation as falsification of a ZK gate invariant without invoking any proof verifier or testing malformed proofs. Scope output as simulation and remove proof/physical conclusions.

title: Archived sitrep presents constant success values as independent attestation
evidence: The report asserts ATTESTED_C5_REAL and health_index 98.6. Traced generator scripts/c5_sharur/sharur_100_conversation_reporters.py:341-345 assigns both literals and PASS without checks; lines 96-100 and 148-152 similarly emit constant sync/isolation successes, serialized by the reporter.
trigger: Reading the archived sitrep as evidence of security or workspace isolation.
impact: The recorded certification and several PASS assertions cannot establish the claimed properties because the generating branches do not measure them. Preserve as unverified historical output rather than attested evidence.

title: Signed integer division can panic instead of returning Critical halt
evidence: Div checks rhs == 0 only, then evaluates lhs / rhs. LoadImm accepts every i64, including i64::MIN.
trigger: LoadImm R1 i64::MIN followed by Div R1 -1.

title: Ledger audit reports HEALTHY without inspecting any ledger
evidence: c5.auditLedger returns constant HEALTHY and compliance Verified JSON. No ledger path, read, hash recomputation, or BFT check occurs. main.rs:142-166 routes workspace/executeCommand directly to this function.

impact: The editor receives a successful integrity/compliance assertion with no evidence.

title: Identity forging truncates existing master seed and is not atomic
evidence: touch(exist_ok=True) followed by open(...,"w") replaces master_seed.enc unconditionally; no existing-identity rejection, temporary-file rename, or fsync. Cross-file consumer seal_bounty_aeon.py:126-129 calls forge_identity after any load exception.
trigger: A caller attempts recovery from a wrong passphrase/decryption error, or process interruption occurs during replacement.
impact: The existing identity can be silently replaced or left unreadable, losing the signing identity needed to verify historical records.

title: Production-labelled dispatcher returns successful work without calling providers
evidence: All three dispatch methods sleep and return fixed SUCCESS results; prompts are never sent and keys/URLs are unused. Header labels this a Production Script; the adjacent MODULE.md:90-98 describes its executable harness.
trigger: Use dispatch_task/run_swarm_campaign for a plan, context analysis, or code mutation.
impact: Results claim planning or mutation completion despite no provider inference or code effect. Scope is this shipped skill harness, not evidence of deployment elsewhere.

evidence: When --bundle is supplied, SHA-256 comparison is conditional on truthy release_bundle metadata. Without that optional metadata the digest is computed and discarded, followed by VERIFIED. CI invokes the script with --bundle (.github/workflows/ci.yml:146).
trigger: Verify any existing bundle against otherwise valid evidence whose manifest has no release_bundle object.
impact: The verified message does not establish that the supplied bundle is the release described by the evidence.

title: Benchmark extrapolates Python loops into isolation guarantees
evidence: Both branches compute the same SHA-256 predicate; the eBPF branch additionally runs empty Python loops. No eBPF, syscall, shared-memory IPC, isolation, or agent termination is exercised. A measured speedup prints that a corrupt agent dies at zero cost.
trigger: Run stress_test and obtain speedup > 2.
impact: The printed success certifies unsupported isolation and zero-cost claims from an intentionally unequal simulation.

title: Aeon verifier trusts the public key supplied by the untrusted manifest
evidence: Lines 206-219 construct VerifyingKey exclusively from sovereign_identity.l0_public_key_b64; lines 227-236 make overall_valid depend on that signature and a literal status. Consumer main.rs:519-537 returns success for overall_valid.
trigger: An arbitrary signer supplies a manifest containing its own public key and a signature over its chosen root.
impact: verify-aeon reports successful kernel attestation for an identity never provisioned or trusted by the operator.

title: Aeon identity, claim count and hardware metadata are outside the signature
evidence: Only hex-decoded merkle_root is passed to vk.verify. aeon_id, total_claims_sealed and hardware_uuid are subsequently returned and printed by main.rs:522-534 without cryptographic binding; signed_payload is unused.
trigger: Change an existing valid manifest's aeon_id, total_claims_sealed or hardware_attestation while retaining its root/signature.
impact: The CLI still certifies the modified manifest and prints unverified metadata alongside the valid signature.

title: Full-spectrum auditor emits PASS and certified measurements without performing checks
evidence: audit_cohort_ring0 sets PASS and assigns atomic/concurrency/biometric claims as strings (lines 80 onward). Formal cohort likewise assigns certification strings; linguistic entropy is a constant (ent=4.967), not calc_shannon_entropy. run_100_agents_audit aggregates these verdicts and persists them as a SITREP.
trigger: Run the advertised audit against a broken or unverified implementation.
impact: Audit artifact claims successful security/formal/physical verification even though the relevant implementation and measurements were never inspected.

title: Deployment script exits successfully after both publication commands fail
evidence: The gh repo create command falls back to git push; neither final failure is checked, and the last echo on line 14 determines a successful shell exit status. No set -e is present.
trigger: Repository creation and fallback push both fail (for example missing authorization or absent master branch).
impact: Caller receives exit 0 and BABYLON-60 Online despite no successful publication.

title: Metadata writes can overwrite another manager’s keys or revocations
