title: Dry-run force-moves the existing release branch
evidence: git commit-tree and git branch -f release/v5.0-clean execute at lines 103-104 before the DRY_RUN exit at lines 127-132.
trigger: Invoke --dry-run while release/v5.0-clean points to a previous prepared release and earlier checks pass.
impact: A validation run replaces an existing release ref and creates a commit, potentially discarding the intended release tip from that branch. No script was run.

title: Second-order belief returns the target belief regardless of observer knowledge
evidence: observer_agent is only checked for membership; method returns query_belief(target_agent,...). run_demo consumes it at line 316 and tests/test_doxastic_kripke_engine.py:86 covers only an observer who witnessed the relevant scenario.
trigger: A target privately sees an object move while a different observer is absent; query the absent observer's belief about the target.
impact: Returns the target's updated private belief even though the observer could not know it. The demonstration cannot establish second-order false-belief reasoning. No deployed security consumer was established.

title: Registry verification succeeds despite stale entries and metadata drift
evidence: sync_skills_json removes purged_skills from entry_map and recomputes metadata, aliases, adjacency and audit vectors, but verify_only returns only len(missing)==0 without comparing the recomputed data with the loaded registry. CLI propagates this boolean to the exit status at line 523.
trigger: Remove an obsolete physical skill or change an existing skill's role/alias while every remaining physical skill already has an entry, then use --verify.
impact: Verification can exit zero while docs/skills.json still contains ghost entries or stale routing metadata. Static control-flow finding; no verifier was executed.

title: Benchmark prints a fixed end-to-end latency attribution it never measures
evidence: print_forensic_report always states that 70% of perceived slowness is due to the framework after successful imports. Measurements only time imports and 10,000 local formatting/template calls; there is no LLM/network or perceived-latency measurement.
trigger: Execute the benchmark in an environment where LangChain is installed, regardless of the measured ratios.
impact: The report presents an unsupported quantitative attribution as a measured conclusion; downstream comparisons may repeat it. This finding concerns generated report evidence, not actual framework performance.

title: Push proceeds when neither biometric gate implementation is available
evidence: The command lookup / Swift-file conditional ends at line 193 without an else rejection; line 197 directly runs git push origin main. This is a direct effect consumer, not merely proposal admission.
trigger: A checkout has local commits ahead of origin/main and neither c5_biometric_gate on PATH nor the Swift source file is available.
impact: The script publishes commits without obtaining the hardware attestation it explicitly requires. The Swift file currently exists, so this is a missing-gate failure-mode defect, not a claim that the current checkout bypassed authentication.

title: Optimizer resolves repository root one directory too low
evidence: parents[3] is 01_KISH_ENGINE for this file. The child is invoked as scripts/c5_thermo/exergy_optimizer_agent.py with that cwd (lines 38-40), but the assigned repository stores it at scripts/c5_thermo/exergy_optimizer_agent.py beneath the repository root. pre_push_ledger_guard.verify_exergy lines 28-36 consumes the returned False.
trigger: The repository pre-push exergy check invokes run_exergy_optimizer in a normal source checkout.
impact: Python cannot open the script under 01_KISH_ENGINE/scripts; the check returns False and prevents pushes regardless of the optimizer result.

title: Attestation verification accepts stale artifacts and an editable self-checksum
evidence: verify_attestation reads every digest from the same saved JSON and hashes those strings, comparing only to another field in that JSON (lines 167-176). It never calls compute_file_sha256, get_git_head_commit, or checks a signature. CLI main --verify directly consumes it and prints validity.
trigger: An input calendar/compliance file or Git HEAD changes after --emit, or a statement is edited and its unkeyed compound hash recomputed.
impact: The verifier reports VÁLIDA (100% Integridad Causal) despite changed source artifacts; it supplies no authenticated provenance.

title: Verification failures still return a successful CLI exit status
evidence: main calls verify_attestation() but ignores the returned boolean; both missing statement (False at line 161) and checksum mismatch (False at line 180) reach normal process termination.
trigger: Automation executes python tools/tamkarum_attestation_engine.py --verify on a missing or inconsistent statement.
impact: Shell/CI callers that check process status receive success even when verification failed.

title: Inbound email acknowledges exhausted webhook delivery failures
evidence: After three failed fetch attempts, the handler only logs and resolves; no rejection, throw, forwarding or durable queue exists in this handler.
trigger: Webhook rejects or remains unavailable for all three attempts.
impact: Email handler reports completion while email payload has not been delivered or durably retained.

title: Thermal budget addition can overflow before admission comparison
evidence: current + cost is used in both comparison and CAS without checked addition.
trigger: After one admitted unit, public try_admit(usize::MAX) overflows.
impact: Debug builds panic; ordinary release overflow can wrap to a small value and admit a cost exceeding max_heat. No external caller for this cost found in src/crates.

title: Draft filenames accept path components from campaign JSON
evidence: lead_id is interpolated directly into output_drafts_dir / filename and write_text; no basename or containment validation.
trigger: An audited/passable campaign lead has an absolute lead_id or ../ segments and --save-drafts is used.
impact: Draft can overwrite a writable text path outside the requested drafts directory; parent directory must exist.

title: Missing Lean oracle is replaced by a numeric heuristic certification
evidence: Missing oracle or launch failure restores Beta when bkm_acc.lower_bound() >= 3600 and gamma agrees (also lines123-125); final output claims native Lean reflection.
trigger: Run example with missing/unlaunchable oracle and threshold-satisfying scenario.
impact: Example can report SingularityCandidateIsolated and native verification without running the formal oracle. This is example evidence, not demonstrated production authorization bypass.

title: Commit polisher invokes nonexistent rewrite script path
evidence: _rewrite_commits invokes scripts/rewrite_commits.py; targeted filesystem read reports absent. Actual matching implementation is scripts/c5_git_utils/rewrite_commits.py.
trigger: Polisher reaches rewrite after reviewer and optimizer succeed.
impact: Rewrite subprocess fails and polisher loops failure recording; configured rewrite functionality does not run.

title: Disconnected Markov output is not strict JSON
evidence: Fallback returns surprisal_bits=float("inf"); CLI json.dumps uses default allow_nan and emits Infinity (lines1920 onward).
trigger: --json requested for disconnected origin/target.
impact: Output advertised as structured JSON cannot be parsed by strict JSON consumers.

title: Shutdown stops consumer before draining its queue
evidence: stop() sets _stop_event before awaiting queue.join(); _worker loops only while that event is unset (line 366).
trigger: Call stop() with at least one queued event before the worker consumes it.
impact: Worker exits without task_done for pending items; stop() and their futures can wait indefinitely.

title: Encrypted retries cannot satisfy ledger idempotency
evidence: event_id derives from plaintext at 489-492; each retry encrypts anew at 496; existing ciphertext is compared byte-for-byte at 433.
trigger: Retry the same LedgerEvent with CORTEX_VAULT_KEY enabled.
impact: Randomized Fernet ciphertext differs, so an otherwise idempotent retry is rejected as a collision; nested rollback then terminates the worker.

title: Rollback is repeated after the transaction has already rolled back
evidence: _execute_insert_tx rolls back in its except block at 476-478; _process unconditionally rolls back again at 505 and closes the connection if that fails.
trigger: Any insert transaction error, such as a SQL CHECK constraint violation.
impact: The second ROLLBACK has no active transaction; the connection is closed and worker fails, leaving other queued futures unresolved. The collision path additionally rolls back at 434 before its exception handler rolls back again.

title: Attestation combines separate database snapshots
evidence: Counts and maxima are selected at 279-285, hashes at 287-289, without BEGIN; verify_chain opens another connection at 302.
trigger: Append commits between those reads while get_state_attestation runs.
impact: Reported totals, roots and integrity flag can describe different ledger states; anchor_to_rekor can publish an internally inconsistent head.

title: License authority falls back to a publicly derivable signing key
evidence: Absent or wrong-length BABYLON_LICENSE_ED25519_SEED falls back to SHA-256 of a source-code literal (98-102), then output is labeled VALID_AUTHENTICATED_LICENSE (115).
trigger: Generate a certificate without an explicitly configured valid signing seed.
impact: Anyone with this source can derive the identical authority key and forge certificates signed with the default key. No runtime verifier consumer was established; finding applies to issued certificate authenticity.

title: Example reports global regularity from hard-coded predicates
evidence: evaluate receives literal false,true,true and an empty evidence string (116-120); the selected branch prints REGULARIDAD GLOBAL CLÁSICA DEMOSTRADA (124).
trigger: Run this example and interpret its verdict as mathematical evidence.
impact: Output asserts a global PDE result without deriving its input predicates from the numerical simulation or a proof; the example overstates its evidence.

title: Shutdown stops before draining accepted transactions
evidence: shutdown sets _stop_event before awaiting writer; loop condition at line 54 exits when set. Sentinel does not override that condition.
trigger: Submit transactions then immediately await shutdown, before writer drains queue.
impact: Accepted auxiliary database writes can be lost while shutdown logs clean completion; queued task counts remain unfinished.

title: Shared /tmp prompt queue follows attacker-controlled symlinks
evidence: QUEUE_FILE is fixed /tmp/moskv_fx_queue.json (181); exists/read_text/write_text follow symlinks with no owner or O_NOFOLLOW checks.
trigger: Another local user precreates this predictable pathname as a symlink to a file writable by host user; user invokes --enqueue.
impact: Host overwrites target file with JSON under its own privileges; same shared queue also permits prompt injection. No runtime exploitation performed.

title: Concurrent prompt producers and consumers lose FIFO updates
evidence: enqueue_prompt and get_next_prompt independently read JSON, modify a list, and write whole file at lines 195 and 206 without locking or atomic replacement.
trigger: Two --enqueue processes overlap, or READY consumes while CLI enqueues.
impact: Last writer loses newly enqueued prompts or restores consumed prompts; readers can see partial JSON and reset queue.

title: History rewrite discards local work before establishing backup
evidence: _ensure_main executes checkout main then reset --hard origin/main; main calls it first (90). No clean-tree check or backup creation exists although header claims preservation.
trigger: Operator runs script with uncommitted main changes or local main commits ahead of origin/main.
impact: Tracked work and local main history are discarded before rewrite validation. This is direct CLI behavior, not inferred downstream execution.

title: State monitor commits unrelated staged changes
evidence: git_sentinel_commit runs git commit without path restriction on existing index, then c5_real_colapso amends at 270; _git ignores return codes and disables signing, commit skips hooks.
trigger: Run monitor with unrelated staged changes present.
impact: Unrelated changes are included in automatic commit/amend without review; failed git commands can still be reported as completed.

title: TCW classifier omits required flanking nucleotide
evidence: Forward branch checks middle C and final A/T but never motif[0] == T; reverse branch checks middle G and first A/T but never final A. Docstring at 88 specifies TCW.
trigger: Pass C>T with context ACA or CCA, or G>A with TGC.
impact: Non-TCW variants are counted as TCW and can change reported enrichment and is_apobec_driven. This finding concerns implemented string predicate, without clinical efficacy claims.

title: Energy and enstrophy truncate squared i64 values to u64
evidence: discrete_enstrophy and discrete_kinetic_energy square in i128 then cast each square to u64 before summation (379,384).
trigger: Form containing a value 4294967296 (2^32).
impact: Its square 2^64 truncates to zero, returning zero energy/enstrophy for a nonzero field; larger sums also overflow u64. Pure arithmetic counterexample, no execution.

title: Physical grid spacing absent from numerical RHS
evidence: Taylor-Green initializer stores point velocities (679,685), grid_spacing_h is 2*pi/n (650), but compute_vorticity returns unscaled d1 differences (703) and compute_rhs uses unscaled curl and curl-adjoint without 1/h or 1/h^2 (796-802).
trigger: Run the stated [0,2pi)^3 velocity simulation at two mesh resolutions with same physical viscosity.
impact: Advection and diffusion rates scale with resolution instead of the configured physical PDE; CFL uses physical h while RHS uses lattice differences. Limited to code discretization consistency.

title: F60 reduction changes the represented value for partial base factors
evidence: reduce divides num by gcd(num,60^scale), but decrements scale only for whole factors of 60 (lines 43–51).
trigger: BA.EXACT dividing numerator 2 by 60 produces F60::new(2,1); gcd=2 divides numerator to 1 without changing scale.
impact: The result becomes 1/60 instead of 1/30; ordinary exact arithmetic is silently corrupted.

title: Division ignores the denominator scale
evidence: BA.EXACT reads numerator register scale but only val2.num; val2.scale is never applied (326–337).
trigger: Divide integer 1 by register containing 1/60 (obtainable by dividing 1 by 60).
impact: Returns 1 rather than 60, corrupting any subsequent arithmetic on fractional operands.

title: Replay digest authenticates only elapsed ticks
evidence: initial hash is constant BABYLON-60-INIT and replay_hash is SHA256(self.c.to_be_bytes()); trace/state bytes never enter either hash (184–192).
trigger: Run different programs or change a traced opcode while preserving final tick count.
impact: Exported proof artifacts have identical replay hashes despite different programs/states; the hash cannot establish replay integrity.

title: Unsupported instructions are silently accepted
evidence: Opcode match fallback is _ => {}; execution then records opcode and advances PC (416–430). Assigned tools/examples/navier_stokes_hunter.b60 uses DAH, LAL, NU at lines 34,43,46, none implemented in this match.
trigger: Run the supplied Navier–Stokes script or mistype an opcode.
impact: Program silently skips arithmetic and branch operations; the supplied example cannot detect its advertised threshold.

title: Script operands can panic the interpreter outside its halt path
evidence: ALLOC unconditionally indexes tokens[1], tokens[2] and coro.r[idx]; similar unchecked reads appear in other opcodes. Register file length is 64 (455).
trigger: Script contains ALLOC alone or ALLOC F60 R64.
impact: Out-of-bounds panic terminates the process without critical_halt/export_artifact diagnostics.

title: Unique query generator inevitably stops making progress
evidence: Both query length and word indices depend exclusively on len(unique_queries); length cycles mod 6 and vocabulary indices mod len(VOCAB).
trigger: Execute the 1000-query benchmark.
impact: The candidate repeats after at most lcm(6,len(VOCAB)) distinct lengths/offsets, fewer than 1000 here. On the first duplicate set size freezes and the while loop repeats forever before inference.

title: Mail migration deletes records belonging to unrelated subdomains
evidence: The zone-wide records list is filtered only by MX type or TXT content v=spf1 (48–58); replacement records target only domain= babylon60.com (62–67).
trigger: Zone includes MX or SPF records for a delegated mail subdomain in the returned records page.
impact: Migration deletes those subdomain mail records and never restores them, disrupting unrelated mail routing and sender authorization.

title: Server binds all interfaces despite announcing loopback
evidence: port is :1234, log announces 127.0.0.1, then http.ListenAndServe(port,mux); handler has no authentication (46–83).
trigger: Start the Go adapter on a host reachable from another machine.
impact: The mock chat endpoint is exposed on all interfaces contrary to its displayed local address; remote clients can submit arbitrary request bodies.

title: Monitor presents constants as live security and treasury telemetry
evidence: load_telemetry_data hardcodes allocation=46.66, gate LOCKED, ring0 NOMINAL, oracle ARMED (51–54); only DB/manifests/calendar are read (57–87). UI adds biometric status, <15ns latency and total legal compliance (126–129).
trigger: Run --once with missing inputs or a failed/unavailable gate.
impact: Operator receives successful-looking hardware/security/compliance status and treasury allocation without observations from those systems; failures cannot change these indicators.

title: Sequence validator accepts an empty normalized sequence
evidence: Nonempty input is checked before upper().strip(); no emptiness check follows. Empty invalid_chars passes, seq_len=0 returns is_valid=True (87–116).
trigger: Call validate_sequence with a nonempty whitespace-only sequence string.
impact: Invalid empty biological input receives a valid result and the digest of empty bytes.

title: Byte-sized fields are emitted as eight-byte stores
evidence: Layout assigns Bool size/alignment (1,1) at 85, but Store/VolatileStore always emit mov qword [rax],rcx at 193–198; Load also uses qword.
trigger: Use the public layout/backend path for a struct containing two Bool fields; its allocation is two bytes.
impact: Generated assembly writes eight bytes for each Bool field, overwriting neighbors and allocated bounds. Existing Sensor example hides this by putting Bool in tail padding.

title: Comment fallback directs audit output without acquiring comments
evidence: On extraction failure, Phase 3b directs generation of SOCINT audit by projecting five vectors from predictable audience sociology (201–203).
trigger: A comments audit cannot retrieve comments within 10 seconds or encounters anti-bot/error responses.
impact: The prescribed fallback substitutes imagined audience reactions for unavailable observations; no explicit labeling requirement separates projections from an actual comments audit.

title: Queue failure handler references an unbound exception
evidence: except sqlite3.Error at line 99 does not bind exc; exc is assigned only if the nested fallback fails at line 115.
trigger: An enqueue fails after db_path has already switched to _fallback_path.
impact: Logging raises UnboundLocalError instead of returning the documented graceful queue failure.

title: Half-open circuit admits every concurrent caller
evidence: can_execute changes OPEN to HALF_OPEN for the first caller, but returns True unconditionally for all subsequent HALF_OPEN callers.
trigger: Concurrent decorated calls arrive after recovery_timeout while the first probe is awaiting its network result.
impact: The recovering endpoint receives concurrent probes rather than the claimed single trial, defeating throttling during recovery.

title: Assimilation target can escape the incoming directory
evidence: CLI --target-name flows unchanged through assimilate_payload to INCOMING_DIR / target_filename and write_text at line 83; no containment validation.
trigger: Invoke assimilate with an absolute path or ../ segments naming an existing writable parent.
impact: The command overwrites files outside its documented incoming forge directory; no remote invocation or production authorization bypass is asserted.

title: Code fence extractor matches a literal backslash instead of a newline
evidence: The regex string contains four escaped backslashes before n, yielding a regex for a literal backslash followed by n rather than a line break. Fallback retains Markdown fences.
trigger: Normal remote output is ```python followed by a newline, Python code, and a closing fence.
impact: Python/JSON fenced responses fail syntax verification, while other extensions can be saved with fence markup intact.

title: Reallocation clears live borrow state without invalidating references
evidence: Alloc blindly inserts Unborrowed into states; existing reference_map entries are retained.
trigger: Alloc R0; BorrowMut R1 from R0; Alloc R0; Free R0. The second Alloc erases Mut(R1), so Free returns Ok while R1 remains mapped.
impact: The example checker loses the outstanding R1 borrow and can accept Free R0 while R1 remains mapped, undermining its demonstrated lifetime guarantee.

title: Certificate panel presents static text as verified hardware attestation
evidence: Step 3 contains a hard-coded VERIFIED token and immutable Secure Enclave signature claims; setStep exposes it directly and launchWorkbench only logs and alerts.
trigger: Open the SCITT Attestation tab without any backend result.
impact: The UI displays a verified certificate without signature or receipt verification. This is a presentation claim defect; no actual protected execution is demonstrated.

title: Consolidation deletes journal rows without saving their replacement
evidence: JournalEntry.load returns only the ID (26-27), merge discards payloads (30-32), save is pass (34-35), then DELETE executes at 51. database.core.connect uses isolation_level=None.
trigger: Call autoconsolidate against a nonempty journal table.
impact: Every selected original entry is deleted with no replacement persisted; autocommit makes deletion durable even before the final commit.

title: YouTube URL and output directory are interpolated into shell commands
evidence: run_cmd uses subprocess.run(shell=True) at 9; URL is interpolated into double quoted command strings at 17, 36 and 42; argv flows directly to fetch_youtube_audit at 53-55.
trigger: Pass a URL or output directory containing shell command substitution or a quote followed by shell syntax.
impact: The shell executes injected commands with the invoking account privileges. Double quotes do not suppress command substitution.

title: Persistent retry deadlines use a clock that resets at reboot
evidence: Worker compares next_retry_at to time.monotonic at 43-54 and stores it at 77; producer pulmones.py:87 stores time.monotonic()+delay in SQLite.
trigger: Reboot after queueing a task when the previous uptime was long.
impact: Persisted deadlines remain in the previous boot clock domain and can postpone retries for the old uptime duration.

title: Fetching retry work does not claim rows atomically
evidence: SELECT at 46-55 has no lease/status update; execution happens at 110 and deletion only at 113 via a separate connection.
trigger: Run two PulmonesWorker processes on the same database and fetch the same ripe batch before either deletes it.
impact: Both workers execute the same queued side effect; there is no ownership claim or deduplication in this worker.

title: Appliance installer copies from a crate-local target directory in a workspace
evidence: REPO_DIR resolves to crates/eridu-infer at 60-61; cargo build executes there at 68 but cp expects crates/eridu-infer/target/release/eridu-infer at 69. Cargo.toml defines the root workspace; .cargo/config.toml has no target-dir override.
trigger: Run provisioning from a clean checkout with cargo available and no crate-local prebuilt binary or CARGO_TARGET_DIR override.
impact: Cargo places the workspace artifact in root target; cp fails under set -e after system power/network settings have already been changed.

title: Master ledger explicitly selects NORMAL durability despite FULL requirement
evidence: BFTMasterLedgerWAL sets PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL at 112, immediately below comments requiring FULL for a master ledger at 110-111; .babylon60rules requires synchronous FULL.
trigger: Use this ledger class for committed transactions and suffer OS/power failure before WAL synchronization.
impact: The configured durability is weaker than the class contract and committed recent transactions may be lost; no crash experiment was run.

title: Telemetry stop cancels the worker without draining pending events
evidence: stop docstring promises draining at 55 but cancels at 57, awaits the cancelled worker and clears it at 62; it never awaits queue.join or consumes remaining items.
trigger: Ingest events and immediately stop before the background worker has consumed them.
impact: Queued events remain unprocessed when stop returns, contrary to the shutdown contract.

title: Attestation test passes even for blocked or failed results
evidence: The test branches only print status and errors at 24-29; it has no assertion about status, receipt or signature anywhere.
trigger: run_chaos_monad returns a failure/error dictionary without raising.
impact: The test succeeds and can give a false regression signal for a broken attestation pipeline.

title: Generated temporary variables collide with circuit inputs
evidence: new_var emits v0, v1, ... without reserving circuit parameter names; compile inserts parameter names verbatim (44-50), and generated Rust uses var_<name> for both inputs and gate outputs (130-144). Grammar accepts v0.
trigger: Compile a circuit with public v0 and statements let x = 1; assert(v0 == x); the first constant output is also v0.
impact: The emitted witness declaration shadows the public input variable and the assertion becomes constant==constant, leaving the intended public-input assertion unenforced.

title: Drug-target affinity cancels the target vector
evidence: bind multiplies bipolar components (56-58); similarity dots them (60-63); affinity returns dot(drug*target,target)/DIMENSION (112-119). Since target_i squared is 1, result is sum(drug_i)/DIMENSION.
trigger: Compute affinity for the same drug against any two registered targets.
impact: All targets receive the same affinity, so this method cannot rank target-specific interactions; this is an algebraic software defect, not a clinical outcome claim.

title: Parallel face-swap jobs share one identity embedding file
evidence: TEMP_EMBEDDINGS_PATH is the fixed /tmp/c5_source_embeddings.npz at line 96; every parent overwrites it at 627 and workers load that same path at 812, without a session path argument or lock.
trigger: Start a second pipeline with different identities after the first writes embeddings but before all first-job workers have loaded them.
impact: Workers can use the other job's identities, mix identities across chunks, or fail while reading a concurrently rewritten NPZ.

title: Worker suppresses encoder failure and can deliver truncated video
evidence: The frame write catches BrokenPipeError/IOError and breaks at 428-432; ffmpeg_proc.wait() at 442 has its return code discarded. The worker returns normally; parent only checks Python child return codes at 700-704 before concatenation.
trigger: FFmpeg exits after writing a partial but parseable chunk, or input decoding stops early.
impact: A worker exits successfully despite missing frames; concat/mux can accept a shorter valid MP4 and pipeline prints DONE without a frame-count check.

title: Media gate ignores ffmpeg measurement failure
evidence: ffmpeg runs with check=False; lines 428-442 parse stderr and evaluate metrics without checking ebur_res.returncode.
trigger: Measurement process emits an in-range loudness/peak summary but exits nonzero (for example after a decode or output failure).
impact: The gate may return verified=True and cache the artifact despite an unsuccessful measurement command.

title: Persistent actor resets its Lamport clock on restart
evidence: Constructor sets lamport_clock=0; _init_db only creates the table (225-241), never reads MAX(lamport_clock); commit_state computes max(local,proof.clock)+1 at 247.
trigger: Reopen a ledger containing clock 100 with a proof clock of 1.
impact: The next row can have clock 2, breaking monotonic ledger order; replaying an identical earlier proof can also collide and silently return sequence -1 (273-275).

title: New face tracks are returned twice on their first frame
evidence: New tracks are appended at lines 215-216 but never added to matched_tracks; the lost-track loop at 219-224 increments their lost count and appends the same face again. c5_face_swap_cli.py:280 consumes tracker.update assignments.
trigger: Any previously unseen detected face with an assigned identity.
impact: The face is processed twice in one frame and starts with lost=1 despite having just been detected, producing redundant swaps and incorrect extrapolation lifetime.

title: Blur framing fails for sources taller than the output aspect ratio
evidence: scaled_h is computed exclusively from target_w/src_w at 279-281; negative y_offset is used directly for the destination slice at 283-284 without fitting/cropping foreground.
trigger: A portrait source such as 1080x2400 with default 1080x1920 output and mode=blur.
impact: The destination slice cannot accommodate the full foreground array, so NumPy assignment raises a shape error and framing aborts.

title: Gate receipts assert verified compliance without evaluating it
evidence: evaluate_and_seal only hashes tick/model/prompt and publishes a digest (62-89); it unconditionally emits EU_AI_ACT_COMPLIANT_ARTICLE_12_14_VERIFIED at 97. server.rs:139 calls this on request content and uses its seal in generated responses.
trigger: Any inference request for which publish succeeds.
impact: A receipt represents regulatory verification and attestation without policy checks, evidence validation, authority signature, or compliance evaluation. This is an unsupported runtime output claim, not evidence of a cryptographic authorization bypass.

title: Receipt hash does not distinguish model/prompt boundaries
evidence: The hash updates concatenate tick bytes, model bytes and prompt bytes at 66-68 without length prefixes or separators.
trigger: Two gates at the same tick evaluate (model="ab", prompt="c") and (model="a", prompt="bc").
impact: Different inference inputs yield identical prompt_hash and attestation_seal without a SHA-256 collision, undermining receipt input binding.

title: Vault consolidation records a fixed session catalogue instead of reading source sessions
evidence: REPORT_PATH and REPORT_FALLBACK are declared but never read; the loop inserts the static UNCONSOLIDATED_SESSIONS into L1/L3 and vault_consolidations, commits at 212, and reports SUCCESS at 224.
trigger: Running consolidation against an empty vault or with source logs missing or differing from the embedded catalogue.
impact: Persistent memory is populated with summaries and consolidation attestations without evidence that those sessions exist or were actually consolidated; subsequent runs skip those IDs.

title: Cancer pipeline emits attested numerical invariants without inputs or computation
evidence: run_cancer_isomorphism_pipeline constructs fixed morphism_preservation=True, spectral_radius_bound=0.021, isomorphism_degree=1:1_DETERMINISTIC and status=ATTESTED at 18-28. CLI accepts only --json.
trigger: Any invocation, including with no cellular model or observations available.
impact: Machine consumers receive fabricated verification status and a numerical bound presented as pipeline results; this supplies no scientific evidence for the asserted invariants.

title: Repository inventory falsely marks every repository as having a README
evidence: GraphQL requests workflows but never a README object; enrichment nevertheless writes has_readme=True unconditionally.
trigger: A queried repository lacks a README.
impact: Downstream repository audits are given a false positive for documentation presence and can skip needed remediation.

title: Array display truncation corrupts the GGUF parse cursor
evidence: The ARRAY branch consumes count.min(10) values then returns that cursor, without skipping remaining elements.
trigger: Load a valid GGUF metadata array containing more than ten elements, such as tokenizer vocabulary.
impact: The next metadata key or tensor descriptor is read from inside the array; ordinary models fail to load or receive incorrect descriptors.

title: Truncated GGUF metadata panics instead of returning an error
evidence: parse_metadata_value directly indexes mmap[cursor] and slices cursor..cursor+N; caller checks the type tag but not its payload.
trigger: A file ends immediately after a UINT8 metadata type tag, or contains a truncated string/scalar payload.
impact: Untrusted model input can panic the inference process rather than produce load_mmap Err.

title: Consolidation discards divergent same-name master ledgers
evidence: _process_master_db returns True when destination already exists (lines 33-35); caller then unconditionally calls _purge_db_file.
trigger: A master ledger exists in ~/.babylon60/dbs and the repository contains a different ledger with the same basename.
impact: Source ledger and sidecars are deleted without comparing, merging, or preserving its records.

title: Copying only SQLite main file loses WAL commits
evidence: shutil.copy2 copies only db_path; _purge_db_file unlinks its -wal and -shm at lines 41-42.
trigger: Consolidate a WAL-mode master ledger with committed pages still in its WAL.
impact: Central copy omits committed transactions, then the source WAL carrying them is removed.

title: Concurrent rate limiter callers reserve the same future slot
evidence: _refill resets _last_refill=now even when it was a future reservation; every deficit caller then sets tokens=0 and last_refill=clock()+wait_s.
trigger: Several threads acquire while the bucket is empty before the first waiting caller wakes.
impact: They all receive approximately the same wait and dispatch together, violating the intended rate bound and increasing upstream throttling.

title: Sensitive routing omits the explicit target from its free-model veto
evidence: candidate_list uses payload.models whenever present; build_chat_payload chooses explicit model as payload.model independently (lines 649-650); sensitive context does not imply enforce_floor at line 732.
trigger: query receives sensitive context_paths, an explicit :free model, and a paid-only models list.
